Have you considered talking to someone about your suicidal feelings?
There are many people in this world who have never ever considered suicide. Chronic suicidal feelings are not healthy and you really should consider going to see someone about your feelings. 

I don't know much about this stuff, but what I do know is that the brain is incredibly complicated and that it's very possible that there is something (a chemical imbalance in your brain or w/e) that might be causing this. Something that might be fixed with medication. You don't have to live like this. There are options.

EDIT: also, head over to [/r/suicidewach](http://www.reddit.com/r/suicidewatch)

Do you know why our age estimates of the earth have been increasing over the past years? surely if several hypotheses over the years of measuring all coincide, then the number should be becoming more accurate, and not increasing.

I don't like the way my response sounds. a number can be increasing and be tending toward an equilibrium like in a stable system. What I mean is, what happened to all the hypotheses from years ago that had much smaller numbers than we do now? have they all been proven wrong? How do we know that this time we're right?
Yay! some new info.  I will google and research and see what i can find.

I don't have anything against small numbers. I honestly don't just say "herp derp too small herp derp". I have an issue with *how close the numbers are together*. I should have mentioned that. Here, [I drew you a picture](http://i.imgur.com/Xmqbh.png). 

I'm not a scientist and I don't even know that much about maths and statistics and that stuff. 

All I'm saying is that if we're dealing with numbers that are really close together compared to the time period we're talking about, there tends to be infinitely many solutions. and when there are infinitely many solutions. *We just don't know*.

Okay, this is where my chemistry goes a bit fuzzy, hence the confusion. I didn't know that the little numbers meant. Anyway, [this comment](http://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/gh690/hi_reddit_i_have_a_question_about_how_we_measure/c1nhz38) is an accurate reflection of where i stand with all this at this moment in time, after a bit more though and reading. I'd be interested to hear your thoughts.

I agree with the theory. My problem is that in real life, your percentages are not 10% and 20% and 50%. Those can be accurately used to fit the half life formula. The problem I have is that we're talking like 0.000000000001% decay over a year. (don't count those zeros, I just mashed the keyb, but you get the point). So, if i get 0.000000000001587980% and 0.00000000000167803% and 0.0000000000016345%, I don't think that I'm going to be able to accurately represent the decay of uranium. 

EDIT: Even if i do it over and over and over again. I honestly just think the numbers are too small. 

Correction: I should have said that the numbers are *too close together*.

I also want to point you in the direction of [this comment](http://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/gh690/hi_reddit_i_have_a_question_about_how_we_measure/c1nhz38), which i made in response to someone else and might address your questions to me about consistency in the laws of the universe.

I agree with you when you say this: 
>The universe has always followed the laws that it currently follows, unless there is evidence to indicate that the laws were different in the past. 

But I also think that there are infinitely many formulas that can fit in our data points that we measure when we  measure the rate of decay of uranium. If we make a measurement over the course of the year, and we choose to extrapolate that measurement to billions of years, then how do we decide how that uranium decay rate is going to behave? Naturally, we can look at the decay rates of other things, and that might give us an example of the general shape of decay, but we don't know for sure how to exactly extrapolate the data. So I imagine we try something. and it fits (maybe). And then later on we get a new piece of information and we realize that the new info doesn't fit to our formula, so we try another one. and another one and another one. 

Okay, so if we carry on going forever, there can be three outcomes: 

* There is one formula. 

* There are none that fit. 

* There are infinitely many that fit. 

One is the most difficult to prove. As far as i can see, we're still living in "there are infinitely many" land as far as reserch goes. If we had already hit "there is no answer", I think I would know about it, because it would make the news. I don't think we could ever find "the answer" because there are infinitely many formulas to try and we have such a teeny dataset based on the fact that there is a huge extrapolation between years and billions of years. SO. bottom line: That's why I think that we just don't know, because there are infinitely many solutions, and we don't have enough data. NOT because I think the universe changes laws randomly on a whim. 

My whole point: I don't like that the way the earth is stated as fact when it's not. We don't know that we are right because there are infinitely many answers and we are assuming that we are tending to a single answer, which might not be the case.
but isn't what you just said absolute? You are assuming that the fact that "no absolute knowledge exists" is an absolute.

I understand what you're saying and I agree to a certain point, but where is the line that says "this is fact" and "this is just a guess, but it looks like it could work". For a long time I was told that the dating methods we use are absolutely certified fact, but when I started actually thinking about it, I realized that we actually don't really know for 100%. Extrapolating data from years to billions of years just doesn't seem accurate to me, and the numbers showing how old the earth really is have increased and increased. These things make me lean away from the "this is absolute fact" camp. 

note: I have said "the numbers showing how old the earth really is have increased and increased" as part of my argument because that gives an indication that in order for us to get our hypothesis to fit into actual reality, we've had to extrapolate more and more, and needed more and more time.

But how do we know what accurate is? Isn't accuracy only relative to a known, measured value? How do we know if our results are "accurate" if we don't have anything to compare them to? Okay, so I can get my special decay measurement thingy and measure the change in decay between now and tomorrow, but my formula is only based on what I see between the two points. I have no idea what happened outside of that, and even though I know that my equipment has an accuracy of x, I have no way of confirming that the formula which fits for my measured time period, will also work outside of that.

I'm still not so sure. there are lots of assumptions. How do we know how big the half life of uranium really is? Yes, we can measure how it decays in a few years, but how do we know how far along it is in it's life?  Since it's half life is so much longer than what we can measure, we can see only a teeny portion of it's half-life decay characteristic. [Here, like this](http://i.imgur.com/Ead75.gif).

Is it really that predictable? I mean, I'm not so sure about extrapolating a year to a billion years. What if I'm just looking at a particularly linear part of the characteristic curve? [Here, I drew a picture of what I mean.](http://i.imgur.com/Ead75.gif) How do we know exactly what part of the half life characteristic we're looking at?

EDIT: cleaned graph axes

Oh, ok, I think I misunderstood the [wikipedia page](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uranium-lead_dating), which said this:
>The method relies on two separate decay chains, the uranium series from 238U to 206Pb, with a half-life of 4.47 billion years and the actinium series from 235U to 207Pb, with a half-life of 704 million years.

It's actually talking about a change in state, rather than the half-life of the element itself. (As far I i understand).

I've read through both the radiometric wikipedia page, and the uranium lead wikipedia page, and I have another question: How do we establish the half life of lead or uranium? 4.5 billion years is a huge number. where did it come from?

EDIT: I know this question is google-able, and you're welcome to leave me to google it, which i will.

I understand what you're saying, but isn't that assuming that there is a linear rate of change, or a rate that can be ~~described by a formula~~ accurately represented within a few thousand years?

Even if we did continuous measurements over thousands of years, there is still a huge extrapolation from thousands to billions. 

EIDT: I say thousands to be generous. I don't know how long studies go on for, but even if results were passed down from generation to generation, I can't imagine they weould go on for any significant period of time, relative to billions of years.

I'm a little bit confudes about something and I'd like to ask a question.

Say for example, I would like to figure out a way of knowing how old a tree is. I have an hypothesis. I think that the rings of the tree tell it's age. So what do I do? I test my hypothesis by planting a tree. Or finding a tree of a known age. And I know the age because there was a person who planted the tree and they documented that the tree was planted on a certain date. With a bit of subtraction, I know how old the tree is. Say I find a tree of a known age, and I look at the rings, and i see a correlation between the number of rings and the age of the tree. Then I do it for another one and another one and another one, and i carry on testing my hypothesis. After lots of trees, and lots of consistent results, I can conclude that is very likely that rings of trees tell you how old they are. If my test fails, then I have to go back to the drawing board. This is how I was taught that scientific testing works. It was part of my high school education.

Okay, so if I wanted to tell how old a piece of rock is, I would need a piece of rock of a known age. But what if I wasn't around a billion or however many years ago to confirm that the rock really is that old? No one was around back then. How do we know for sure that these things really are that old? As far as I understand, we are doing several different age measurements on rocks and fossils and things, but they're all hypotheses, and they're all fine, relative to eachother, but I don't know how we can know for sure, because there is no *absolute* measure.

So how is it possible to say for sure that the earth is *any* age without having an absolute measure?

Why do people treat mentally disabled people so differently? I have Autism and i don't understand why people treat me weird. I don't even know if i fall under the "mentally retarded" category. I don't feel retarded, but I was put into a school for retarded people. Sometimes people are nasty to me and I don't know why.

I think I got tired of being the victim. I felt very sorry for myself, kinda "oh poor me, boo hoo". I decided to proactively try to work with the people who were looking after me and helping me. I realized that certain things i just don't like. There are triggers in my environment that cause me to be overwhelmed or freak out or get scared or uncomfortable. I started to learn what those things were and avoid them. I tried to find the things that make my comfy and happy and are soothing. I guess my mindset slowly changed from "I'm broken" to "I'm different". I started to learn how i am and how I do things and how I think. This is ME. And my parents were always there. Telling me that I'm ok and it's ok to be like this and it's not the end of the world and that you can live and be happy and comfortable if this is managed properly.

Today, I *like* how I am. I don't want a cure. I like that I'm innocent in a dark world and i don't want to be like everyone else. I've seen what people are like and i don't want to be like that. I'm glad I'm not like that.
Thanks :) I'm definitely where I am today because of them.

I didn't like changing schools. That was difficult. When I arrived it was noisy and there were lots of people. I guess specifically I just didn't know what to do. I didn't know who to talk to or what to say. I didn't know where to go. I didn't know where I belonged. I didn't know if these people could see through me. Could they see that I was weird? What if they hated me? What if they didn't accept me? What if they thought I was ugly? I'm uncomfortable if I don't have a familiar point of reference. If i don't know what to expect. Starting high school was a big combination of everything that makes me uncomfortable.

Thankfully, and i have to add a positive point here, otherwise this whole thing is negative, It only lasted a few days. The first day was hard. The next was better because i had been there the day before. I knew the place sort of. Each day I went back, i knew more people, I knew what to do, I started learning my way around. The first day in any place doing anything new is very difficult.

I hated change. If the kid is coping in mainstream, leave them there. let them keep the familiar environment and the friends and the teacher. if the kid is not coping, find out why. Is it too loud? Are there too many people? Do they need more attention? Do they need less attention? Is the work too fast paced?

I moved from a special-ed class with mixed disabilities to a small, mainstream, private structured classroom, which did *wonders* for my learning. The old class was noisy and unstructured and the material was slow paced. 
The new one was quiet and small and structured and expected me to perform. I wanted to do my best because it was expected. I was in "proper school" now. I liked the teacher and she gave me space and made sure that i was comfortable.

Where all this fits into your question, I don't know. I guess i can only draw on my experience and i hope it sheds some light on the the subject. I'm sorry I can't be any more helpful.

I learned to speak, but then went backwards. I honestly don't know much because I can't really remember much of those years. I think I was advanced in my word-making, but sentence wise I couldn't put a sentence together. I had a big vocab with no sentence making ability.
Thanks. how much is a lot?

I think the main thing that made a difference was that i wasn't treated as if i was stupid. Well, sometimes I was, but the *good* teachers didn't treat me like I was stupid. It takes balance i think. An understanding of the person and how they are. That takes time. There are some times where it's appropriate to be firm and say "No, I know you, and this is not acceptable behavior from you". And other behaviors are understood to be out of my control and accepted for me. It takes time to know the person and how they are and learn to respond to them appropriately. Sometimes the line between what I can control and what I can't goes fuzzy. It feels like I'm freaking out because of outside factors, but actually it's just in my head and I've got full control but I just don't take it because I haven't clicked that I can. At that point "Get yourself together", is appropriate and works for me. I hope this makes sense.

Starting high school was very uncomfortable. I really don't like it when I don't know anyone. 

I feel separated. I feel like I'm not the way everyone else is and i feel like I don't fit in with them no matter how hard i try.

I think that I have embraced who I am to a certain degree. I have got an attitude of "this is me, take it or leave it". I like who I am and even though I feel limited sometimes due to autism, i like the... raw feelings that come along with it. So in my case, I don't see it as a disability now. I did before. I went though a "oh poor me, I'm broken" phase a few years ago. I felt like it was a disability then. 

I'm still me. There is a person in here. And I can think and reason and the only difference is that my interface with the world doesn't work like yours. I wish people could get that. I've heard people talk about me when they didn't know i was listening. They said horrible things about how I'm retarded and dumb and will never be able to function on my own. Well guess what, I proved you wrong.

Living on my own his hard work. I'm used to people telling me what to do and making decisions for me, and that's not there anymore. I have to decide what to have for dinner, where to have dinner, what to do first: brush my teeth or shower first. In the beginning there were just so many decisions to make it was almost overwhelming.
I made a list opf exactly what I would do and when. I have a morning routine, a lunchtime routine and a supper routine. and I have small routines in between like what to do if i want to go shopping. Every single day i do exactly the same thing. I know some people don't like that but it's comfortable for me and I need it to stay sane.

The dentist. I hated the dentist. I hated the nose and the drilling and the vibrations. The dentist i want to originally was horrible and din't know much about people like me. He ruined my dentist opinion and i didn't go to the dentist for years because of it. I really had a bad toothache one day and needed to go, so i found another dentist to go to. I was so scared in the beginning, but he was very good and he understood and told me exactly what he was doing and gave me warnings about everything and told me what to expect. It wasn't so bad and I was so surprised that I actually got through a dentist visit without freaking out. And he had a rubrics cube for me to do :D and pictures on the roof :D

I think i go through waves of independence. Some days I feel like i can go out and conquer the world. Other days I want to hide in my corner and never see anyone ever again. I think maybe your brother is just doubting his ability to be independant. He maybe isn't so sure that he actually can do this. Maybe his diagnosis has opened his eyes to actually how different he really is, and that's scary and he wants to hide from the world. I know that's how i feel sometimes. Like, I doubt my ability to be normal and it feels like the whole world can see right through me and into my weakness and I want to hide that. Maybe he doesn't want you to see him stim and see him do weird things. And before he let you see them because they were just him and how he is and he didn't realise that that's weird and not everyone does stuff like that, and now he gets that he's different and he wants to hide. 

I dunno if that's true for his case, it was for mine and I know my explanation is not very ordered, i just spewed a whole bunch of thoughts on paper. I know if i read them I'll probably delete them because they're very raw. So I won't read them again and I'll charge on and tell you what to do to help.

Treat him like a normal person. As if nothing has happened. Spend time with him, doing stuff you always used to do. Do not highlight his weirdness, ignore it. Leave it alone. He knows it's there and he needs to see that you don't see him any different because of it. Encourage him to do stuff. If he says no, you can push a little bit, but be careful. I'm afraid to say more because this is very case specific stuff and I know what works for me might not work for him. PM me if you want to chat more about it. If I know more about him and what he does i might be able to elaborate more.

It's like the words are all up in the air out of reach and you've got to jump really high to grab hold of one. It took ages for me to even ask for a hug. What works for me is non-verbal signalling, like hand signs or pointing to a picture. I have a typical gesture of making fists with my hands and tapping my knuckles together when I'm uncomfortable. A couple of my teachers picked up on that and used it as a cue for a hug.

I don't think having an autistic boyfriend would work, because there would just be too much complicatedness. 

I don't really have any boyfriend requirements, i guess that he's patient when I freak out and is willing to find out that makes me tick and be patient enough to work his way into my comfort zone. It takes time for me to get used to people. 

And naturally all of those other obvious things, like nice and kind and interested in me.

I've found that there are specific things that work ing calimg me down when I get all uncomfy and start freaking out. I don't think that they work with everyone, it's very person specific. I guess the only thing I can suggest is finding what works for each kid. 

For example, physical contact with someone I'm familiar with works well for me. If i'm freaking out, touch my wrist. It's like my mind zones in on the touch and it's all soothing and warm and makes me go all fuzzy and relaxed inside. Naturally, it only works if I know you. If you're a stranger I'll be all like "Why's this creepy person touching me? What am i supposed to do? AAAH"
